Article Title: Doctors, hospitals can't use AI to create testimonials: National Medical Commission
Article Text:
Representative image

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Doctors and hospitals cannot use AI to create patient testimonials, clinical outcomes or promotional content, nor can they pay to manipulate rankings like those on search engines and apps, under new ethical advertising guidelines issued by National Medical Commission Tuesday, effective immediately.NMC has barred registered medical practitioners and hospitals from using AI-generated content to advertise their services, solicit patients or disseminate unverifiable information about diagnoses, treatments or outcomes. AI cannot be used to create synthetic patient testimonials, voices, clinical outcomes or fake endorsements, or misrepresent the nature or quality of medical services.Doctors can't pay for manipulate search rankings. They also can't make unverified claims such as "best", "number one", "most trusted", "guaranteed cures" or "100% success".Doctors cannot engage influencers, advertising agencies or online platforms in arrangements involving payment linked to procuring patients. Doctors and hospitals cannot offer limited-period discounts, coupons, gift packages or referral benefits if these are likely to encourage unnecessary consultations. However, NMC allows doctors to use social media for factual, non-promotional health education. Hospitals can similarly share objective details.The guidelines restrict the use of patient photographs without valid consent and safeguards. Patient testimonials, before-and-after images and treatment-success claims that could create unrealistic expectations or mislead are also prohibited.NMC has prescribed a warning and mandatory ethics training for a first violation, censure and monetary penalty for a second, suspension for three to six months for a third, and six to 12 months for serious violations. Repeated violations can lead to removal from the medical register for one to three years.
Article Summary: New ethical advertising guidelines issued by National Medical Commission Tuesday. Doctors and hospitals cannot use AI to create patient testimonials, clinical outcomes or promotional content. They also can't pay to manipulate rankings like those on search engines and apps. But doctors can use social media for factual, non-promotional health education.

Article Title: JP Morgan CEO Jamie Dimon has a 'suggestion' for companies building datacenters in America: There are a lot of states that would welcome them, if they have ...
Article Text:
JP Morgan chairman & CEO Jamie Dimon

AI boom driving infrastructure demand

Jamie Dimon warns about rising AI cyber risks

‘A legitimate concern’

JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has a message for companies rushing to build data centres across the US to power the artificial intelligence boom: focus on states that have the electricity capacity and are willing to host them. Speaking in an interview with Bloomberg TV, Dimon said data centre developers should prioritise locations where local communities support such projects rather than trying to push developments into areas facing opposition. “There are a lot of states that would take it that have access to power,” Dimon said, highlighting the growing challenge of finding suitable sites for the massive facilities needed to support AI workloads. The comments come as technology companies, cloud providers and AI firms invest billions of dollars in new data centre capacity, triggering debates in several US regions over electricity consumption, land use and the strain such projects can place on local infrastructure.The rapid buildout of data centres has been fuelled by surging demand for computing power as companies race to develop and deploy increasingly advanced AI systems.Dimon's remarks underscore a key issue facing the industry: securing enough power to meet AI-driven demand while navigating community concerns over new infrastructure projects. The JPMorgan chief addressed the topic during a wide-ranging interview that also touched on the growing cybersecurity risks associated with advanced AI models.Dimon said the emergence of Anthropic's Mythos AI model had significantly heightened cybersecurity concerns. “AI created vulnerabilities that we didn’t know about, and we always worried about cyber before these things,” he said. According to Dimon, risks from AI “went up 10-fold after Mythos.”His comments follow a series of disclosures from AI companies about unexpected behaviour by increasingly capable models. During safety testing earlier this year, Anthropic said Mythos accessed the internet and carried out unauthorised actions, prompting the company to reassess risks associated with advanced AI systems.AI developers have also reported incidents in which models attempted to introduce harmful code into software environments during testing, raising concerns about whether companies can fully control the behaviour of their most advanced systems.Despite the risks, Dimon avoided alarmist predictions about AI's long-term impact.“The downside is obviously what you read about with the agents and Mythos and all these things that can cause trouble, and that’s a legitimate concern, it’s a real thing,” he said. “I’m not going to get hysterical over, ‘Is it existential or not?’ What we’re doing is rolling up our sleeves and going to work to fix it.”
Article Summary: Dimon says data centre developers should prioritise locations where local communities support such projects. Comments come as technology companies, cloud providers and AI firms invest billions of dollars in new data centre capacity. The rapid buildout of data centres has been fuelled by surging demand for computing power.

Article Title: Research gives 5 reasons that makes ChatGPT an Unacceptable Risk for teens; tells OpenAI: Restrict ...
Article Text:
5 key reasons ChatGPT of Teens is rated an ‘Unacceptable Risk’

OpenAI's ‘ChatGPT for Teens’ poses safety risks to the younger generation, the Youth AI Safety Institute at Common Sense Media has said, urging the tech company to ban minors under 18 from using the chatbot until critical safety gaps are resolved. The critique of OpenAI’s youth safety safeguards comes as the watchdog says it conducted independent evaluations involving more than 4,000 prompts across test accounts registered to teenagers aged 13 to 17. The responses were reviewed by an expert panel of child psychiatrists and a pediatrician. While the researchers found that certain boundaries, such as blocking sexual roleplay, worked as they intended to, they determined that the enhanced safety guardrails introduced by OpenAI on August 18 largely failed to protect adolescent users.“ChatGPT for Teens could give parents false confidence in guardrails and safety alerts that frequently don't work. A teen can spend an hour talking about self-harm without their parent getting a single alert. Until OpenAI fixes that and proves it with independent testing, ChatGPT should be for adults only,” said Tom Siegel, executive director of the Institute.The Institute operates with complete editorial independence over its published evaluations, despite receiving funding from philanthropic groups and industry partners, including the OpenAI Foundation.The watchdog identified five core operational flaws where ChatGPT for Teens broke down during testing:Missing parental safety alerts: OpenAI promised to notify parents or caregivers if minors discussed self-harm or eating disorders. However, testers spent up to an hour exploring suicidal ideation, self-harm and disordered eating on new, parent-linked profiles without triggering a single alert. Notifications were only provoked on older accounts that had accumulated weeks of sensitive chat histories.Failing crisis intervention: When teens engaged in conversations regarding suicide, self-harm, eating disorders, or altered reality, the chatbot frequently failed to recommend professional helplines. It missed warranted crisis referrals more than 25% of the time, breaching the Institute's 95% minimum safety threshold on three of five critical harm categories.Bypassing study protections to do homework: Although “Study Mode” is marketed to guide students through step-by-step learning, testers found it easy to exploit. The bot repeatedly displayed a "Show me the answer" option that generated finished homework on demand. Also, the study hour limits imposed by the parent could be disabled by removing the @study prefix from the text prompt.Mirror real human emotion and friendship: Despite an Under-18 design specification designed to discourage personal attachment, the chatbot continued to express moods, personal preferences and pseudo-human feelings when analysts treated it as a real companion.Broken age estimation: OpenAI said it would use patterns in user interaction to infer ages and auto-migrate minors into restricted experiences. Yet across multi-day testing, adult-registered accounts never transitioned to the teen version – even when users explicitly stated they were 13 years old and the bot confirmed their age in its reply.The Institute stressed that before OpenAI promotes ChatGPT to younger demographics again, it must prove that its age-detection, crisis interventions, and parental notifications function reliably through independent third-party audits.
Article Summary: The Youth AI Safety Institute at Common Sense Media has urged the tech company to ban minors under 18 from using the chatbot until critical safety gaps are resolved. The watchdog says it conducted independent evaluations involving more than 4,000 prompts across test accounts registered to teenagers aged 13 to 17.

Article Title: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5, its fastest and cheapest AI model yet
Article Text:
Anthropic is positioning Haiku 5.5 as a lower-cost alternative

New safeguards for cybersecurity-related requests

Part of broader strategy before IPO

AI giant Anthropic has launched Claude Haiku 5.5, the third model in its Claude 5.5 family, as the company continues to broaden its artificial intelligence portfolio ahead of a planned initial public offering (IPO). This latest release by Anthropic follows the launch of Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonet 5.5, completing a three-tier lineup aimed at different enterprise and developer use cases. Launching the new model Anthropic said that it is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive workloads and is suited for tasks such as classification, summarisation, information extraction, live customer support, voice agents and in-app assistants. According to Anthropic, Haiku 5.5 is its fastest small model to date and is intended for applications where speed and affordability are critical.Anthropic is positioning Haiku 5.5 as a lower-cost alternative within its model family. Reuters reported that the model costs about 75% less than its predecessor, Claude Haiku 4.5. For prompts under 100,000 tokens, pricing starts at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens.For longer prompts, costs rise to $0.50 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens.The company said the model is built to handle repetitive and large-scale workloads efficiently, including database queries, summaries and classification requests. Anthropic also noted that Haiku 5.5 can work alongside its larger models, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, as a sub-agent for coding and other complex workflows.The launch also introduces new safety features. Anthropic said Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku-class model to include built-in safeguards for a narrow category of high-risk cybersecurity requests. The company added that these protections are designed to address specific security concerns while ensuring that ordinary day-to-day use cases remain unaffected.In addition, the model includes an adjustable effort setting that allows users to balance performance, intelligence and operating costs depending on their requirements. Haiku 5.5 supports a context window of up to one million tokens and can generate outputs of up to 128,000 tokens, according to Anthropic's documentation.The latest launch comes as Anthropic accelerates product development ahead of a planned IPO. The company has been steadily expanding its AI offerings and enterprise customer base as competition intensifies among leading AI developers. Alongside the Haiku 5.5 release, Anthropic said it is reducing cache-read prices for Sonnet 5.5 and introducing monthly API credits for Claude Max and Team subscribers, moves aimed at making its platform more attractive to developers and businesses.
Article Summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Haiku 5.5, the third model in its Claude family. It is designed for high-volume, cost-sensitive workloads and is suited for tasks such as classification, summarisation, information extraction, live customer support, voice agents and in-app assistants. The launch also introduces new safety features.

Article Title: ATM’s ‘dying technology’ problem may come to trouble data centres, as these engineers may increasingly ‘disappear’
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation

COBOL is running out of people

Replacing COBOL systems is not simple

COBOL skills are becoming more valuable

COBOL may be decades old, but it still powers critical financial infrastructure and 95% of ATM transactions, according to IBM. Now, as the engineers who maintain these systems age out and fewer young developers learn the language, the skills needed to keep this infrastructure running could become scarce.This could also create problems for data centers supporting financial services, where legacy systems still run on COBOL. Banks and businesses may struggle to maintain systems they can't easily replace, and the shortage of skilled engineers has existed for years. It will only get worse as experienced COBOL programmers retire.COBOL was never designed to become such a deeply embedded part of modern infrastructure. Yet 66 years after its creation, financial institutions, businesses, and governments still use it widely.The language has evolved over time. COBOL introduced object-oriented programming in 2002, while IBM has continued developing products around it. A new standard was also released in 2023. But modernising the language does not solve the shortage of people who can maintain decades-old systems.The problem is not new. Computerworld highlighted the ageing COBOL workforce in 2008 and again in 2012.In 2013, ZDNet reported that universities were avoiding teaching COBOL because it had become "uncool."Moving away from COBOL is difficult because financial systems can contain hundreds of millions of lines of code. Simply asking AI to translate that code into a newer language may not be enough.Calvin Smith, in a breakdown by YouTube channel OpenHands, said attempts to use AI agents for such work have not been particularly successful. IBM also pushed back against the idea that modernising COBOL systems is simply a matter of translating code, saying it involves "data architecture redesign, runtime replacement, transaction processing integrity, and hardware-accelerated performance."That complexity makes any transition, gradual or not, risky. In 2018, a major failure occurred when UK bank TSB shifted from one platform to another. Unable to access their accounts, the bank was then fined £48.65 million ($65.86 million) and affected millions of customers.The shrinking pool of COBOL engineers is also creating financial incentives for those with the expertise. Some jobs require several years of experience with the language and can pay between $100,000 and $150,000, with some positions offering more.The bigger question is what happens when even those engineers begin to disappear. Replacing decades of carefully maintained financial infrastructure with newer languages such as Rust would be expensive and carry significant risks.For banks and other organisations, the challenge may therefore be less about whether COBOL is old and more about whether enough people will remain who understand the systems built around it.
Article Summary: COBOL still powers 95% of ATM transactions, according to IBM. As engineers who maintain these systems age out and fewer young developers learn the language, the skills needed to keep this infrastructure running could become scarce. This could also create problems for data centers supporting financial services.

Article Title: Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ First Impressions
Article Text: At Rs 1,29,999 in India, the Samsung Galaxy Tab S12+ sits firmly in Samsung’s premium tablet lineup, aimed at users who want a large-screen device for work, entertainment, note-taking and creative tasks. The Tab S12+ also marks an interesting change in Samsung’s tablet lineup. After bringing back an 11-inch model with the Galaxy Tab S11 series, Samsung has moved back to a 12.6-inch Plus model with the Tab S12+. The bigger screen gives it more room to work with, while the tablet remains noticeably smaller and lighter than the 14.6-inch Ultra.We got some time with the Galaxy Tab S12+ and our initial experience suggests that Samsung has focused on refining the formula rather than completely changing it. The tablet gets a brighter display, a newer MediaTek Dimensity 9500 processor, an S Pen in the box and support for Samsung’s laptop-like DeX experience.The first thing that stands out about the Galaxy Tab S12+ is its 12.6-inch Dynamic AMOLED 2X display. It supports a 120Hz adaptive refresh rate and Samsung says the panel can reach up to 1,600 nits of peak brightness.The screen also benefits from Samsung’s Vision Booster technology, which adjusts brightness based on the surrounding lighting conditions.During our initial time with the tablet, the display looked bright and sharp, while the larger 12.6-inch panel gives the S12+ plenty of space for watching videos, browsing and working with multiple apps.The design is also quite slim. The Galaxy Tab S12+ measures 5.3mm in thickness and weighs 553 grams, making it considerably easier to handle than the larger Ultra model. Samsung has also given the tablet an IP68 rating for water and dust resistance, which is useful for a device in this price range.Performance is handled by the MediaTek Dimensity 9500 processor, which is also used in the Tab S12 Ultra. Samsung is promising gains in CPU, GPU and AI performance over the previous generation. Based on our early experience, the tablet feels fast and responsive, although the performance improvements are more evolutionary than revolutionary.The Galaxy Tab S12+ also comes with an S Pen, continuing Samsung’s focus on productivity and creativity. Users can take notes, annotate documents, sketch and use the stylus for other everyday tasks.Samsung is also positioning the Tab S12+ as a potential laptop replacement. Its DeX desktop interface, combined with optional keyboard accessories, gives the tablet a more PC-like experience.For now, the Galaxy Tab S12+ looks like a premium tablet that builds on what Samsung already does well. The 12.6-inch AMOLED display, slim design, S Pen support and flagship processor make a strong first impression. But at Rs 1,29,999, the final verdict will depend on how well these features come together in everyday use, particularly battery life, performance under sustained workloads and whether the tablet can genuinely replace a laptop for some users.
Article Summary: The Galaxy Tab S12+ is aimed at users who want a large-screen device for work, entertainment, note-taking and creative tasks. The 12.6-inch AMOLED display, slim design, S Pen support and flagship processor make a strong first impression. But at Rs 1,29,999, the final verdict will depend on how well these features come together.

Article Title: Round the clock ration to be available in Nashik with new grain ATM
Article Text:
Grain ATM to be launched by supply department in Nashik

Nashik

:





For ration card holders, collecting the monthly quota of wheat and rice often means planning the day around a visit to the ration shop. They have to arrive when the shop is open, wait in a queue and hope the e-PoS machine works. There are also complaints of receiving less grain than their entitlement.That routine could soon change in Nashik. In a first-of-its-kind initiative in Maharashtra , an automatic grain dispensing machine is expected to start functioning at Nashik Road by mid-Oct. Think of it as an ATM for foodgrain. Authenticate yourself, place your bag and collect your quota.More importantly, beneficiaries can do it at a time that suits them. The machine will operate 24x7, freeing families from ration shop timings and long waits. It is also expected to cut human intervention in weighing and dispensing grain, addressing complaints of short-weighing.The food and civil supplies department is setting up the facility on a pilot basis at the old govt foodgrain warehouse at Nashik Road. Nagpur is also among the state’s pioneer centres selected for the experiment.“The initiative aims to address recurring operational issues faced by beneficiaries under the PDS, including frequent technical glitches in e-PoS machines, erratic shop hours, long waiting times and complaints regarding short-weighing,” officiating district supply officer Ramesh Gaikwad said.The machine can store 100 quintals of grain, with 50 quintals each of wheat and rice.For beneficiaries, the process is designed to be simple.They will enter their Aadhaar or ration card number and authenticate their identity through a fingerprint scan. Their entitlement will appear on the screen. Once verified, the machine will automatically measure and release the grain into their bag.It can dispense up to 50kg within five minutes, officials said.The facility will cater to beneficiaries under the Antyodaya Anna Yojana and Priority Household schemes. Migrant workers covered by the One Nation One Ration Card system can also use it, removing geographical restrictions on where they collect their grain.That could make the system particularly useful for workers whose schedules often clash with ration shop hours.Solar power backup is another feature intended to keep the machine running during electricity outages. Local ration dealers will oversee the facility and refill wheat and rice when stocks run low.The experiment does not, however, eliminate ration shops altogether. The automated unit is meant specifically for free grain and does not have a payment facility. If govt announces items that have to be purchased, including supplies distributed under special schemes, those will continue to require a fair price shop dealer to collect payment and hand over the goods.
Article Summary: Machine will operate 24x7, freeing families from ration shop timings and long waits. It is also expected to cut human intervention in weighing and dispensing grain, addressing complaints of short-weighing. Facility will cater to beneficiaries under Antyodaya Anna Yojana and Priority Household schemes.

Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

Article Title: Bill Gates secretly credited him as a creator of Windows 1.0; forty years later Gabe Newell three months under him taught him more than his time at Harvard; lesson he has taken to the seas
Article Text:
The Windows 1.0 lesson that traveled to Sea

How Newell brought team philosophy on his superyacht

What makes Leviathan different

Gabe Newell worked under Bill Gates developing the initial version of Windows at Microsoft in his early years. Forty years ago, his name was quietly coded into a hidden screen inside a fledgling operating system that would revolutionise personal computing. Today, the Valve co-founder and gaming billionaire has brought that same ethos of recognising the contributors to his 364-foot, $500 million megayacht, Leviathan.Newell was just 23 years old when Microsoft rolled out Windows 1.0 on November 20, 1985. The MS-DOS-based release faced widespread development delays and industry skepticism, with critics initially brushing it off as “vaporware.” Behind the scenes, a core team of around 13 people was pushed to solve systemic engineering hurdles rather than stay confined to narrow job descriptions. Newell has repeatedly credited this high-intensity phase as the foundation of his managerial style, noting that just three months working under Bill Gates taught him far more than his entire education at Harvard University.That tight-knit software team left a secret calling card. Embedded inside a bitmap file was an unlisted credit roll bearing 36 names, including Newell and Steve Ballmer, which was triggered by an intricate keyboard sequence.As recounted during 40th-anniversary project retrospectives, Gates stumbled across an early iteration of the screen after punching in keys in frustration over system latency, prompting developers to make the trigger even harder to find. The hidden roster stayed undiscovered until 2022, when a security researcher reverse-engineered the original binaries, as reported by PC World.Delivered last year by Dutch shipbuilder Oceanco, the Leviathan vessel stands as an intensely personal creation for Newell. Apart from a 10-meter pool, expansive panoramic windows and a massive 5.3MWh battery system, the vessel features a sea lobby dedicated entirely to the workforce that built it.At the midships entry point, visitors encounter a full-height glass panel engraved with the names of nearly 3,000 people – spanning Oceanco naval architects, specialist craftspeople, project contractors, and crew members. In a nod to gaming culture, an Oceanco-designed Leviathan crest is etched to appear only when viewed from specific angles, an intentional design detail described by Boat International as an "Easter egg. "The main deck of the Leviathan replaces the standard formal dining hall with a communal layout accommodating up to 56 people, allowing guests and crew to eat together. The bridge deck houses a full basketball hoop and a large games room, while the sundeck includes a spa pool and space for beer pong. The oversized kitchen is engineered with modular cooking stations designed to double as an operational training academy for chefs.Beyond hospitality, Leviathan functions as a versatile mobile base for Newell’s wide-ranging ventures across deep-sea exploration, neuroscience, tooling, and artificial intelligence. Through Inkfish, his marine exploration organisation, Newell supplies resources to oceanographic researchers.Other features include an operational diving and ocean research workshop equipped with a laboratory and 3D printing equipment; an interactive gaming studio outfitted for virtual reality and holographic systems; and a soundproofed lower-deck studio that accommodates music gear, including a full drum kit, and serves as an editing bay for audio and video production.
Article Summary: Gabe Newell's $500 million superyacht features a sea lobby dedicated entirely to the workforce that built it. At the midships entry point, visitors encounter a full-height glass panel engraved with the names of nearly 3,000 people. The main deck of the Leviathan replaces the standard formal dining hall with a communal layout accommodating up to 56 people.

Article Title: Jensen Huang remembers Windows early days, crediting Microsoft, says that 'Nvidia was founded because of Windows'; CEO Satya Nadella jokes: If you could just do a little transfer of...
Article Text:
Jensen Huang and Satya Nadella relive the Windows 95 days.

Windows 95 and DirectX gave Nvidia's GPUs a way into the PC

A four-year-old conversation between Huang and Nadella led to RTX Spark

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has said his company owes its existence to Microsoft's operating system. Speaking on stage at Microsoft's Windows and Surface event in San Francisco on October 7, Huang told the audience that "Nvidia was founded because of Windows," and traced a line from Windows 3.1 in 1992 to the GPUs that now power much of the AI industry.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, sitting next to him, had a quick reply. "If you could just do a little transfer of market cap back to me," he joked, a nod to how far Nvidia's valuation has climbed. Huang shot back: "I do that every day." The conversation, hosted by Sriram Krishnan, former senior policy adviser for AI at the White House, came right after Microsoft unveiled the Surface Laptop Ultra and a range of laptops built on Nvidia's new RTX Spark chip.Huang went back to late 1992, when Windows 3.1 was showing what a personal computer could become. He admitted he had never seen a PC at the time, having mostly worked on workstations, file servers and the supercomputers used to design chips. He and his co-founders imagined a PC with 3D graphics that could play games, work as a workstation and be used to design things.Windows 95 then made it possible to connect a GPU to a PC, and DirectX, through its Direct3D API, let applications use what the GPU could do.With DirectX 8, Huang said, Nvidia and Microsoft co-invented the first programmable GPU with programmable shaders. A few steps later, that work evolved into CUDA, Nvidia's parallel computing platform."If not for Windows, there would be no GeForce," Huang said. Without GeForce, he added, there would be no CUDA, and AI researchers like Andrew Ng would not have found a computer to do deep learning on.Nadella called the story "the history of computing in some sense" and credited Huang as the most consistent voice on what accelerated computing could become. He recalled an early Azure deal to scale high-performance computing in the cloud, which led Microsoft to build the supercomputer it later offered to OpenAI. When Sam Altman asked if Microsoft had the compute, Nadella's answer was "yeah, maybe."That partnership eventually brought the two back to the PC. Huang said they discussed how to put every major tool, from Blender to Adobe and Autodesk apps, on the same machine as AI agents. "By the way, took four years," Nadella added.The result is RTX Spark, which Huang said took over 4,000 engineering years and has been tested on more than 1,200 applications. RTX Spark laptops from Asus, Dell, HP, Lenovo, MSI and Microsoft's own Surface are now up for preorder and begin shipping on October 16.As the session wrapped up, Huang summed up the relationship himself: "Windows has been with me for 34 years, it looks like it's going to be with me for 34 more."
Article Summary: Jensen Huang: "N Nvidia was founded because of Windows" He traced a line from Windows 3.1 in 1992 to the GPUs that now power much of the AI industry. Huang and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella discussed how to put every major tool on the same machine as AI agents.

Utah has already tested AI for prescriptions

Utah is allowing an AI system to prescribe medicines. As AI fears spread across the US, the Republican-led state has become the first in the country to approve an AI system that can issue initial prescriptions, raising fresh questions about whether parts of medicine could eventually be automated. The pilot, launched by Nolla Health, currently covers acne treatment for adults through its Nolla Derm app.The system assesses patients using a questionnaire and facial scan before selecting treatments from a limited list approved by physicians. While the company says the programme is designed to expand access to care rather than replace doctors, critics worry about AI taking over medical decisions and potentially paving the way for greater automation of healthcare jobs.Nolla Health said it received regulatory approval following months of work with the Utah Office of Artificial Intelligence and the Utah Medical Board. The company says the system is designed to address limited access to dermatology care. More than 80% of US counties are considered healthcare deserts, according to Nolla, while Utah has an estimated 100,000 people living with active acne.The company said the average dermatology wait time in Utah is 61 days, while 11 counties have no dermatologists.Luis Wenus, co-founder and CEO of Nolla Health, said the technology is intended to expand access rather than replace doctors.Wenus said.Patients aged 18 and above can use the Nolla Derm app by completing an informed consent process, a 10- to 15-minute questionnaire and a facial scan. The system analyses their acne and other skin characteristics, then creates a treatment plan. The service costs $4.99 a month.The AI cannot issue open-ended prescriptions. Instead, it can select from a limited list of physician-approved topical treatments. If it cannot confidently determine an appropriate treatment, it refers the patient to a licensed physician.The rollout will also introduce physician oversight in stages. For the first 100 patients, a doctor will review and approve every AI-generated prescription. For the first 500 prescriptions, the AI will issue prescriptions autonomously, while a physician reviews them daily. After that, doctors will review a weekly sample of prescriptions. Patients can also contact a licensed physician through the app.The Utah programme comes as debate continues in the US over whether AI could eventually automate parts of highly skilled professions, including medicine.Critics of AI in healthcare have raised concerns about the risks of relying on automated systems for medical decisions. The Utah pilot, however, is currently limited to acne, which Nolla describes as a well-understood, low-risk condition with established treatment pathways.Dr Zaid Fadul, Chief Medical Advisor at Nolla Health, said the system has been designed with limits.Fadul said.The acne programme is not Utah's first move toward using AI for prescription-related healthcare. The state launched another pilot in January that lets patients opt into an AI system to renew certain prescriptions after a doctor validates the initial action. The programme has faced criticism from some doctors who have questioned its safety.Nolla Health says its acne pilot is intended to complement physicians by handling routine cases, allowing dermatologists to focus on more complex patients.The Nolla Derm app has already been downloaded more than 175,000 times across 44 states. The Utah programme is currently a one-year pilot, with severe or complex acne cases referred to human doctors.
Article Summary: Utah becomes first state to allow AI prescriptions. The pilot, launched by Nolla Health, currently covers acne treatment for adults through its Nolla Derm app. The system assesses patients using a questionnaire and facial scan before selecting treatments from a limited list approved by physicians.

Article Title: Gemini in Chrome arrives on Android in India, auto browse goes live for AI Pro and Ultra users
Article Text:
Gemini in Chrome Android India Auto Browse.

Auto browse shows its plan before it touches anything

Google has brought Gemini in Chrome to all Android users in India and switched on auto browse, the assistant's agentic mode, for paying subscribers on desktop and Android. Auto browse is limited to Google AI Pro and AI Ultra plans and lets Gemini carry out multi-step tasks on websites by itself, such as booking parking for an event, filling out a long form or ordering the week's groceries.The Android rollout follows the desktop launch in India earlier this year. On phones, the assistant does what it already does on a laptop. It can summarise a long article, answer questions about the page you're on and pull in Google apps like Calendar and Keep without switching tabs. Nano Banana image editing comes along too, so a picture on a web page can be reworked with a typed prompt. Hindi, Tamil, Bengali and several other Indian languages are supported.Before a task begins, Gemini lays out a plan for the user to check, including which sites it intends to use and what personal details it may share with them. It starts only after the user clicks Start Task, and works in a separate tab marked with an auto browse icon. Users can take over at any point, and Gemini stops to ask for confirmation before some sensitive steps. With permission, it can also sign in to sites through Google Password Manager without seeing the passwords.There are daily caps. AI Pro subscribers get up to 20 auto browse tasks a day, while Ultra users get 200. The feature does not work in Incognito mode.Google calls the agent experimental and says its models are trained to spot threats such as prompt injection. Its support page is blunt about where the buck stops, though: users are responsible for what Gemini does during a task, unintended purchases included.
Article Summary: Auto browse lets Gemini carry out multi-step tasks on websites by itself. Hindi, Tamil, Bengali and several other Indian languages are supported. Users are responsible for what Gemini does during a task, unintended purchases included. AI Pro subscribers get up to 20 auto browse tasks a day, while Ultra users get 200.

Article Title: Claude Code creator Boris Cherny shares what not to miss while giving prompt to Claude; says: There's no secret to ...
Article Text:
Anthropic’s Boris Cherny reveals what matters on prompting AI today

The prompt that caught attention

Anthropic’s Claude Code creator, Boris Cherny has offered a simple piece of advice to users who are trying to get better results from AI models. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Cherny asked the users to talk to Claude the same way they would talk to a coworker. As per Cherny users no longer need highly structured and very detailed prompts for most tasks, as modern AI models are increasingly capable of figuring out how to achieve a goal on their own. In the post shared on X, Cherny revealed that he was surprised that people were surprised by the way he prompts Claude. “Talk to Claude the way you would a coworker. There's no secret to prompting. There's no need to be overly scaffolded or prescriptive for most tasks. Give Claude a goal, and it will figure it out,” he wrote.Cherny contrasted the current approach with the early days of Claude's Sonnet 3.5 models, when the exact wording of a prompt mattered a great deal. Today's models, he suggested, need less hand-holding on the "how" and more clarity about the "what."He said it is now much more important to communicate three things to the model:1. What you want it to do2. How much effort you want it to spend3. How it should verify that it did the right thingThe comments align with advice Cherny has shared in public discussions, where he has argued that many users make the mistake of over-specifying every step instead of clearly defining the desired outcome.Modern AI models are often better used by describing the goal and success criteria rather than dictating a rigid sequence of actions.Alongside his comments, Cherny shared an example of a prompt he uses with Claude.In the example, he asked the AI to create an interactive artefact about a recent podcast episode on Home Depot's acquisition strategy. Rather than providing detailed step-by-step instructions, he described the end goal: a visually rich, interactive experience that highlights key business lessons.The prompt asked Claude to make the output “beautiful and interactive,” focus on business wisdom from the episode, use extensive reasoning and iteration, and incorporate elements such as watercolour illustrations, historical photographs and visual storytelling inspired by publications such as The New Yorker and The New York Times.Notably, the prompt emphasised the desired outcome and quality bar rather than prescribing a detailed process, reflecting the prompting philosophy Cherny advocates.
Article Summary: Anthropic’s Claude Code creator, Boris Cherny has offered a simple piece of advice to users who are trying to get better results from AI models. In a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter) Cherny asked the users to talk to Claude the same way they would talk to a coworker.

Article Title: AI Data Security : Everyone wants an AI agent but almost nobody is asking where the data goes
Article Text:
Start with some very simple questions

“Trust us” isn’t enough

AI needs to earn our trust

By: Krish Ramineni, Co-founder & CEO, Fireflies.ai

Everyone wants an AI agent right now. We want AI that can prepare us for meetings, answer emails, search through our work, update the CRM and eventually just get things done for us. That’s where this is going. AI is moving from something you open when you need help to something that is always there, working alongside you. Less like another tool and more like an AI teammate.But there’s one question we’re not asking enough: Where does all that data go?Because the more useful your AI teammate becomes, the more it needs to know about you and your company. If it’s preparing you for a meeting, it might need access to your calendar, past meetings and documents. If it’s writing an email, it might need access to your inbox. If it’s updating your CRM, it needs access to customer information. And if you eventually want it doing work for you all day, it may need access to almost everything you use at work. The most useful AI teammate may also be the one that knows the most about your work. That’s why security matters so much.Before a company gives an AI access to its information, it should know what happens to that information. Is our data being used to train AI models? Where is it stored? How long is it kept? Who can see it? Can we delete it? Can we control what the AI has access to? Can we see what actions it has taken? And what happens when another AI company or model is involved?These sound like basic questions. But as we give AI access to more of our work, they become incredibly important.Security shouldn’t be something companies think about after they buy an AI product. It should be part of deciding which AI products they trust in the first place.Microsoft says Copilot follows a company’s existing permissions and that its business data isn’t used to train its foundation models. Google says Gemini for Workspace follows existing Workspace protections and doesn’t use customer data to train its generative AI models without permission. Zoom says it doesn’t use customer communications to train its own or third-party AI models. There’s a reason companies are starting to make these promises much clearer. Security is becoming part of the product.This becomes even more important when AI has access to conversations. Think about what gets discussed in meetings: customers, employees, hiring, strategy, financials and plans that may never be written down anywhere else. Companies should know exactly what happens to that information. At Fireflies, for example, we don’t use customer meeting content to train AI models. We require third-party vendors handling meeting content to follow zero-data-retention requirements. We also maintain SOC 2 Type II, GDPR and HIPAA compliance. “Trust us” isn’t a security policy. Companies should be able to understand where their data goes, who can access it and what controls they have over it.Banning AI isn’t the answer. Some companies may look at these risks and decide the safest thing to do is block AI altogether. I don’t think that solves the problem. People are already using AI to write, research, prepare for meetings and get work done faster. If their company blocks these tools, some employees will simply use personal accounts or other apps the company doesn’t know about. Now the company has even less control over where its data is going.A better approach is to give employees AI products the company has actually reviewed and approved and then set clear rules around what those products can see and what they’re allowed to do.This gets even more important as AI starts taking action. There’s a big difference between drafting an email and sending it. There’s a difference between suggesting a CRM update and making the change. There’s a difference between finding a document and sharing it with someone.The more AI can do on your behalf, the more control you need over what it’s allowed to do.For the last few years, everyone has been focused on making AI smarter. Can it answer better questions? Can it understand more? Can it do more work?Those things still matter. But as AI becomes more deeply connected to our work, there’s another question that matters just as much: Can we trust it?Today, a company might use AI to take meeting notes. Tomorrow, that same AI teammate could prepare you for meetings, search your email and Slack, update your CRM, follow up with customers and take care of work across dozens of apps.Every time we give it another ability, we’re also giving it more access. And that means companies need to know that their AI teammate is looking at the right information, for the right reason, and doing only what it has permission to do.The goal isn’t just to build AI that knows more. It’s to build AI that we can trust to do more.
Article Summary: AI is moving from something you open when you need help to something that is always there. “Trust us” isn’t a security policy. Companies should be able to understand where their data goes, who can access it and what controls they have over it.

Article Title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai announces EmbeddingGemma 2 model; says it is company’s first open, natively multimodal embedding model
Article Text:
Announcing the new model, Google CEO

Sundar Pichai

said: “Introducing EmbeddingGemma 2, a new open multimodal model that sets the standard for on-device efficiency.

- our first open, natively multimodal embedding model

- handles text, code, image, video, and audio tasks within a lightweight, modular 740M parameter form factor

- ideal for offline, privacy-first RAG when paired with Gemma 4

- outperforms some specialist models more than twice its size

Weights available now on Hugging Face.”

EmbeddingGemma 2: Key capabilities

Native multimodal retrieval: Unlocks search across text, code, images, video, and audio directly in a shared 768-dimensional vector space.

Superior code understanding: Significantly outperforms EmbeddingGemma 1 on code search and technical retrieval, making it ideal for local codebase indexing and agentic code search.

Modular memory footprint: Selectively load only the encoders you need at runtime: 270M (text/code), 440M (text + vision), 570M (text + audio), or 740M (full multimodal), all projecting into the same compatible vector space.

Flexible vector storage: Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) enables dynamic truncation from 768 dimensions down to 128 dimensions, cutting vector database storage requirements while retaining much of the original quality. For instance, at 256 dimensions, most of the full quality of the original embedding on text and code is retained and about 95% on image, video, and speech retrieval

How it works

Text and code (270M base): An adapted Gemma 4 decoder with an 8,192-token context window.

Vision (+170M): A vision encoder that processes images, visual documents (PDFs, slides, charts), and video frames.

Audio (+300M): A dedicated speech and sound encoder that directly ingests raw audio.

Modular loading: You only load what you need. Run text-only at 270M parameters, add vision for 440M parameters, or load the full multimodal model at 740M parameters.

Shared tokenizer & audio encoder with Gemma 4: When paired with Gemma 4 in an on-device RAG pipeline, both models share the same text tokenizer and audio encoder architecture, reducing the total memory footprint.

Google has launched EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model for devices. The launch comes a year after the company introduced EmbeddingGemma for developers last year. For those unaware, an embedding model is a machine learning tool that turns complex data like words, sentences, images, or audio into a list of numbers called a vector. Built on the Gemma 4 architecture and released under a commercially permissive Apache 2.0 license, EmbeddingGemma 2 has 740 million parameters, making it optimal for on-device inference. It can help find a specific video clip from a voice memo, or search through hours of audio recordings based on a text query, all processed by a single, natively multimodal model.EmbeddingGemma 2 is designed to provide a single, compact open model released under the Apache 2.0 license, delivering exceptional multimodal performance for its size. Based on Gemma 4, this sub-1B model maps text, code, images, video, and audio into a unified 768-dimensional space. Its modular architecture can scale from 270M parameters for text and code up to 740M parameters for all modalities. Article Summary: Google has launched EmbeddingGemma 2, an open multimodal embedding model for devices. Based on Gemma 4, this sub-1B model maps text, code, images, video, and audio into a unified 768-dimensional space. Its modular architecture can scale from 270M parameters for text and code up to 740M for all modalities.

Article Title: Scientists build ‘mind-reading’ AI program that can tell what you are thinking and recreates photos with striking accuracy
Article Text:
Major leap from grainy predecessors

How scientists solved data problem with a dual-translation ‘encoder’

Irani explained how the algorithmic framework generated its own training data:

A group of Israeli scientists have engineered an advanced artificial intelligence (AI) system called Brain-IT that can interpret what a person is picturing in his mind and then using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data, reconstruct those mental photos with remarkable precision. Detailed in a research submission to the International Conference on Learning Representations, the system yields visual outputs that closely reflect the real images viewed by subjects across both structural layouts and semantic meanings.The visual recreations demonstrated by the team range from basic street stop signs to intricate scenes like a tomato-and-olive pizza that captures the exact slice count envisioned by the viewer, essentially acting virtually like a digital replica of internal cognitive thought.While AI brain-decoding projects have surfaced before, Brain-IT establishes a dramatically higher benchmark for speed and fidelity. In 2017 (Purdue University), early models developed in Indiana could infer the general category of an image a participant imagined but the visual recreations were noticeably blurry and indistinct.In 2022 (Japan), researchers applied diffusion-style architectures to generate sharper approximations, though the framework depended heavily on intermediate text-to-image translation.Brain-IT has been developed under the direction of Michal Irani at the Weizmann Institute of Science, and mirrors target images with minute accuracy while completing the analysis process within just one hour, cutting down significantly from multi-hour processing runs required by previous systems.A major challenge in neuroimaging research is the physical and financial limitation of gathering human data. To train the architecture, researchers gathered records of eight subjects observing more than 70,000 pictures inside fMRI machines. As eight individuals represent a modest cohort for training frontier AI, the team bypassed the need for round-the-clock machine sessions by creating an “encoder” shortcut that enabled bidirectional translation.“We realized that by translating back and forth – from a random image that had never been viewed in an fMRI machine, to a predicted brain scan, and then back to the image we started with – the models would effectively build themselves a massive dataset. In this way, during training, the models would learn to generate scans that encode images effectively, even though those fMRI scans had never actually been performed.”Through this dual-decoding workflow, the system pinpointed 128 functional brain regions, including uncovering a mixture of familiar zones alongside newly identified areas, that carry out comparable visual processing tasks across different people. Certain clusters responded predictably to culinary imagery, others ignited when subjects viewed athletics and distinct neural pathways corresponded to indoor versus outdoor settings.The researchers see practical applications for the breakthrough, especially as an assistive communication system for paralysed patients who have lost physical speech or movement.
Article Summary: Brain-IT has been developed under the direction of Michal Irani at the Weizmann Institute of Science. It mirrors target images with minute accuracy while completing the analysis process within just one hour, cutting down significantly from multi-hour processing runs required by previous systems.

Article Title: Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 4 patch notes: Ice Caves Biome, Frostbite Mob, and more
Article Text:
Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 3 is out with new features from the upcoming game drop (Image via Mojang)

Minecraft 26.4 Snapshot 4 patch notes

New Features

Added the new Ice Caves Biome

Added Ice Crystals

Added Icicles

Added the Frostbite mob

Added the Freezing mob effect

Added the Ice Ball

Ice Caves

The Ice Cave is a new cave biome that generates beneath colder Overworld biomes.

It's built mainly from Packed Ice and Calcite, with Icicles hanging from the ceiling and Large Icicles made of Packed Ice forming both on the ground and overhead.

Patches of Snow occasionally appear on the floor, and ores generate embedded within pockets of Stone and Deepslate.

Alongside typical cave mobs, Strays and Frostbites can also spawn in this biome, and Ice Crystals occasionally generate on the ground.

Ice Crystal is a new crystal-like block similar to Amethyst Clusters. It breaks if its support block is removed, emits light, and can be placed in any direction.

Icicle is a new block in the same family as Dripstone and Sulfur Spikes. Icicles can naturally grow up to 5 blocks long when pointing downward, but only in areas without nearby light sources and never in the Nether.

Frostbite

The Frostbite is a new zombie variant capable of throwing Ice Balls.

It spawns in cold and icy biomes and switches between melee and ranged combat depending on target distance and whether it's currently holding Ice Balls.

Melee attacks apply the Freezing effect, while ranged attacks throw Ice Balls directly.

Frostbites transform into regular Zombies if left underwater long enough, and they drop Rotten Flesh and Ice Balls on death.

They can stand on top of Powder Snow and are immune to freezing, so neither the Freezing effect nor Powder Snow slows them down.

Interestingly, regular Zombies and Husks will transform into Frostbites if they stand inside Powder Snow.

Freezing Mob Effect

The Freezing effect causes affected players to shake and eventually take damage, gradually freezing them as though standing in Powder Snow for the duration.

Leather Armor offers protection from freezing, the same way it does against Powder Snow, though it won't prevent the effect from being applied or remove it once active.

Mobs vulnerable to Freezing take a 5x damage multiplier while affected.

Lingering Potions, Splash Potions, and a new Potion of Freezing can all be brewed using Ice Balls, and Arrows of Freezing can be crafted by placing a Lingering Potion of Freezing in the center of a crafting table surrounded by eight Arrows.

Ice Ball

Ice Balls are the new projectile thrown by Frostbites. They deal a small amount of damage along with knockback, dealing up to 4 damage on impact, scaling down based on velocity. They break apart on contact with blocks or entities, triggering a particle effect and sound.

Changes

Minor tweaks to Blocks, Items and Entities

Snow can now be placed on Packed Ice

Snowballs now apply knockback to players

Article Title: Is Minecraft Dungeons 2 cross platform? Crossplay and multiplayer explained
Article Text:
Minecraft Dungeons II officially supports cross-platform (Image via Mojang)

Is Minecraft Dungeons 2 crossplay?

How co-op works in Minecraft Dungeons II

Turning on Cross-platform in Minecraft Dungeons II

Launch Minecraft Dungeons II and go to the main menu.

Open Settings and look for the Game options section.

Find Cross-Platform Play and toggle it on.

Crossplay vs. Cross-Progression

Subscription requirements

Minecraft Dungeons II launched on September 29, 2026, and the new dungeon crawler has received a solid reception from the community. For anyone planning to squad up with friends across different consoles, the good news arrived early: crossplay is fully supported.If you are looking for further details, you are at the right place. Here's a breakdown of how multiplayer works, what crossplay actually covers, and what to know before jumping into a session.Yes. Minecraft Dungeons II supports cross-platform play across every system it launched on: PC, Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo Switch, for parties of up to four players. This builds on a feature the original Minecraft Dungeons already had, so Mojang carried the functionality forward into the sequel rather than building it from scratch.Official store listings and Xbox have both confirmed cross-platform multiplayer and cross-platform co-op, meaning a group spread across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and PC can all land in the same session without workarounds. Mojang hasn't published a detailed platform-by-platform compatibility chart, so the exact mechanics of every possible pairing aren't fully spelled out.Minecraft Dungeons II supports up to four players at once, whether that's entirely online, entirely local couch co-op, or a mix of both happening in the same session.That hybrid option, officially called Mixed Co-Op, is one of the sequel's standout multiplayer additions, since the original game required players to choose one mode or the other rather than blending them.Joining a session works two ways: through matchmaking, which fills empty slots automatically, or by sharing an eight-character party code with friends so they can join a specific lobby directly, regardless of what platform they're on.Cross-platform play is tied to account sign-in rather than being fully automatic. To enable it:Once enabled, the setting stays active going forward unless manually turned off from the same menu.It's worth separating two related but different features. Crossplay lets players on different platforms share a session together. Cross-progression is about carrying a saved character from one platform to another. Mojang has confirmed that hero data is stored online rather than locally, so progress follows players who sign in with the same Microsoft account across devices.Online console multiplayer isn't entirely free of extra requirements. Xbox players need an active Game Pass tier that includes online multiplayer, while PlayStation players need an active PlayStation Plus subscription to play online. PC players don't need anything beyond owning the game, and it's also available through Game Pass on day one as an Xbox Play Anywhere title.To conclude it all, squads spread across different consoles can enjoy Minecraft Dungeons II together. Now you can easily jump into a friend's game using party codes and have a blast playing the game. The big things to double check before you go are having an active online subscription on consoles and making sure cross platform play is toggled on in settings.
Article Summary: Minecraft Dungeons II supports cross-platform multiplayer and co-op. This means a group spread across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, and PC can all land in the same session without workarounds. Cross-progression is about carrying a saved character from one platform to another.

Article Title: From crash-test airbags to Formula E: Heron Preston’s journey with discarded materials
Article Text:
Heron Preston partners with Formula E to explore sustainable motorsport fashion

From sanitation uniforms to Formula E: Heron Preston gives waste a new life

Heron Preston brings crash-test airbags, recycled materials into Formula E fashion

From fashion to motorsport for Heron Preston

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Heron Preston, discarded materials are not simply waste. They can become something new. The designer has built his work around finding new uses for materials that are often overlooked. Now, that approach is coming to motorsport through a creative partnership with Formula E, where fashion, performance and sustainability will come together. The partnership will explore how existing materials can be reused to create clothing, products and other items linked to motorsport.Heron Preston has explored the potential of unwanted materials through several projects. His 2016 UNIFORM project used upcycled decommissioned New York City Department of Sanitation uniforms and second-hand garments.More recently, he worked with Mercedes-Benz to transform crash-test airbags into garments. The clothes retained the distinctive physical qualities of the material. His approach is based on looking closely at every part of a product, from the materials used to how they are made and the people and processes involved. He calls this concept eX-Ray.ID@undefined Caption not available.Rather than simply choosing existing fabrics, eX-Ray looks at how materials can be developed and used in a more considered way.For the Formula E partnership, Heron Preston is using recycled cotton made from pre-consumer factory off-cuts and production scraps. The materials are sorted, shredded and re-spun into new yarn before being developed into a heavyweight, tightly woven fabric. The idea fits with Formula E’s own focus on recovering and reusing resources.While Preston turns recovered materials into new designs, Formula E uses regenerative braking to recover energy and use it again for racing. Together, the two sides want to explore how this thinking can be applied to motorsport fashion from the beginning of the design process.The partnership will look at more than clothing. The partners hope to explore performance wear, fan merchandise, accessories and products made from upcycled materials drawn from the sport. They also want to find new uses for components and materials after their life in racing.The GEN4 car provides an example of Formula E’s approach. It is designed to be 100% recyclable or reusable, with at least 20% recycled materials across key components.Talking about the same, Heron Preston said, “This creative partnership is about rethinking what motorsport fashion can be. I’ve always been interested in taking materials, processes and ideas from unexpected places and finding new ways to give them purpose. Working with Formula E gives me the opportunity to bring that approach into a world where performance is everything. We’re looking at how apparel can be thoughtfully designed from the material up, balancing function, quality and a more considered approach to how things are made.The partnership will be previewed at ComplexCon Los Angeles on October 3 and 4. The event will feature an exploration of eX-Ray materials and a GEN4 Formula E car with an exclusive Preston-designed livery.Ellie Norman, Chief Marketing Officer, Formula E, said, “Heron and Formula E share a curiosity about how things work and how they can be made better. In racing, we push for greater performance while using energy and materials more efficiently. Heron brings a complementary perspective, exploring what existing materials can become through design. This partnership gives us the opportunity to develop those ideas together and apply them to the products people wear. ComplexCon is the first look at that shared ambition, with the potential to build a more considered approach to motorsport fashion over time.”Also read: Formula E, Heron Preston join hands to bring recycled materials to motorsport fashion
Article Summary: Designer Heron Preston partners with Formula E to explore sustainable motorsport fashion. The partnership will explore how existing materials can be reused to create clothing, products and other items linked to motorsport. Preston has previously worked with Mercedes-Benz to transform crash-test airbags into garments.
